name: What's the difference between painting and refinishing kitchen cabinets?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between painting and refinishing kitchen cabinets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Painting kitchen cabinets involves applying a new coat of paint over the existing finish after proper cleaning and priming. This changes the color and updates the look relatively quickly and cost-effectively. Refinishing, on the other hand, typically involves stripping the cabinets down to the bare wood, repairing any damage, and then applying a new stain, clear coat, or solid color finish. While more labor-intensive and costly, refinishing can be ideal for restoring the natural wood grain or for significantly altering the cabinet's original appearance. Frasheski Construction offers both services, allowing you to choose the best option based on your budget and desired outcome.
acceptedAnswer.description: Painting applies new color over existing finish, while refinishing strips cabinets to bare wood for a new stain or finish. Refinishing is more intensive.
